    <div class="sk-about-copy">
      <p class="sk-about-intro">
        I’m an undergraduate chemistry student at KAIST, conducting research in <a class="sk-lab-link" href="https://wooyoun.kaist.ac.kr/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Prof. Woo Youn Kim’s group<span class="sk-link-icon" aria-hidden="true"></span><span class="visually-hidden"> website</span></a>. My current work combines molecular generative modeling with nonequilibrium statistical mechanics to estimate free-energy differences for molecular conformational ensembles.
      </p>
      <p class="sk-about-intro">
        My research experience spans experimental materials chemistry, computational reaction mechanisms, and molecular machine learning. Across these areas, I’m interested in how molecular structure, local environments, and physical constraints shape chemical behavior.
      </p>
      <p class="sk-about-intro">
        In the long term, I hope to apply these approaches to biological problems, including the molecular mechanisms of Alzheimer’s disease and the dynamics of intrinsically disordered proteins.
      </p>

  <section class="sk-about-section" id="research-experiences">
    <h2>Research Experience</h2>
    <div class="sk-entry-list">
      <article class="sk-entry sk-entry-plain">
        <div class="sk-entry-body">
          <div class="sk-entry-header">
            <div>
              <h3><a class="sk-lab-link" href="https://wooyoun.kaist.ac.kr/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Intelligent Chemistry Lab<span class="sk-link-icon" aria-hidden="true"></span><span class="visually-hidden"> website</span></a> <span class="sk-entry-separator">&middot;</span> KAIST</h3>
              <p class="sk-entry-role">Undergraduate Researcher</p>
              <p class="sk-entry-advisor">Advisor: Prof. Woo Youn Kim</p>
            </div>
            <div class="sk-entry-meta">
              <span>Dec. 2025 - Present</span>
            </div>
          </div>
          <h4 class="sk-entry-subheading">Neural Free-Energy Estimation for Molecular Ensembles</h4>
          <ul class="sk-entry-bullets">
            <li>Developing a free-energy estimation framework that uses a stochastic-interpolant model to propose transport paths between a harmonic reference and molecular Boltzmann distributions, with free-energy differences estimated from endpoint densities and forward–reverse path probabilities using Bennett acceptance ratio (BAR).</li>
            <li>Adapted and retrained DiTMC for Boltzmann-weighted ensemble generation and built the main inference pipeline, including transport kernels, work calculations, reverse-start sampling, BAR estimation, and diagnostic analyses.</li>
          </ul>
          <h4 class="sk-entry-subheading">Full-Atom Antibody Design with Antigen Flexibility</h4>
          <ul class="sk-entry-bullets">
            <li>Investigated full-atom antibody design accounting for antigen flexibility and induced fit with an E(3)-equivariant generative framework.</li>
            <li>Designed and implemented auxiliary losses for atomic clashes and backbone and side-chain geometry, accounting for valid disulfide bonds; developed visualization and validation tools to assess structural accuracy and physical plausibility.</li>
          </ul>
          <h4 class="sk-entry-subheading">AD-Agent: Mechanism-Aware Drug Repurposing for Alzheimer’s Disease</h4>
          <ul class="sk-entry-bullets">
            <li>Investigated mechanism-guided drug repurposing for Alzheimer’s disease using multi-agent reasoning.</li>
            <li>Implemented OpenTargets retrieval functions to integrate mechanistic and clinical evidence with traceable sources.</li>
          </ul>
        </div>
      </article>

      <article class="sk-entry sk-entry-plain">
        <div class="sk-entry-body">
          <div class="sk-entry-header">
            <div>
              <h3><a class="sk-lab-link" href="https://baik-laboratory.com/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Baik Group<span class="sk-link-icon" aria-hidden="true"></span><span class="visually-hidden"> website</span></a> <span class="sk-entry-separator">&middot;</span> KAIST</h3>
              <p class="sk-entry-role">Undergraduate Researcher</p>
              <p class="sk-entry-advisor">Advisor: Prof. Mu-Hyun Baik</p>
            </div>
            <div class="sk-entry-meta">
              <span>Jan. 2024 - Dec. 2025</span>
            </div>
          </div>
          <h4 class="sk-entry-subheading">Brønsted Acid-Assisted Solid-State [2+2] Photocycloaddition</h4>
          <p class="sk-entry-advisor">Collaboration: Prof. Tehshik P. Yoon, University of Wisconsin–Madison</p>
          <ul class="sk-entry-bullets">
            <li>Investigated how the local molecular environment and water influence selectivity and reactivity using DFT, molecular dynamics, and QM/MM calculations.</li>
            <li>Applied explicit-environment modeling to reproduce the observed diastereoselectivity that conventional DFT solvation models could not capture. <a href="#photocycloaddition-manuscript">Manuscript in preparation.</a></li>
          </ul>
          <h4 class="sk-entry-subheading">Enantioselective Olefin 1,2-Arylamination with Chiral Indenyl–Rh Catalysts</h4>
          <p class="sk-entry-advisor">Collaboration: Prof. Simon B. Blakey, Emory University</p>
          <ul class="sk-entry-bullets">
            <li>Investigated indenyl effects and how N-protecting groups modulate nitrogen nucleophilicity and chemoselectivity between arylamination and aziridination using DFT calculations.</li>
            <li>Proposed additional ligand controls, including saturated indenyl derivatives, to test the model of asymmetric orbital interactions underlying the indenyl effect. <a href="#arylamination-publication">Published in ACS Catalysis (2026).</a></li>
          </ul>
        </div>
      </article>

      <article class="sk-entry sk-entry-plain">
        <div class="sk-entry-body">
          <div class="sk-entry-header">
            <div>
              <h3><a class="sk-lab-link" href="https://yoon.kaist.ac.kr/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Soft Material Assembly Group<span class="sk-link-icon" aria-hidden="true"></span><span class="visually-hidden"> website</span></a> <span class="sk-entry-separator">&middot;</span> KAIST</h3>
              <p class="sk-entry-role">Undergraduate Researcher</p>
              <p class="sk-entry-advisor">Advisor: Prof. Dong Ki Yoon</p>
            </div>
            <div class="sk-entry-meta">
              <span>Jun. 2023 - Dec. 2023</span>
            </div>
          </div>
          <h4 class="sk-entry-subheading">Tunable Electrical Conductance Anisotropy in MOF–Polymer Composites</h4>
          <ul class="sk-entry-bullets">
            <li>Synthesized oxidation-sensitive Cu<sub>3</sub>(HHTP)<sub>2</sub> and its derivatives, maintaining material quality and consistency for conductive MOF–polymer composites.</li>
            <li>Optimized voltage conditions for electric-field alignment of MOFs in a polymer matrix while avoiding solvent evaporation and material shortage in the ITO film. <a href="#mof-publication">Published in Small (2024); featured on the front cover.</a></li>
            <li>Also investigated MOF–polymer composites as selective gas sensors.</li>
          </ul>
        </div>
      </article>

      <article class="sk-entry sk-entry-plain">
        <div class="sk-entry-body">
          <div class="sk-entry-header">
            <div>
              <h3>Choi Group <span class="sk-entry-separator">&middot;</span> KSA</h3>
              <p class="sk-entry-role">Student Researcher</p>
              <p class="sk-entry-advisor">Advisor: Prof. Eun Young Choi</p>
            </div>
            <div class="sk-entry-meta">
              <span>Apr. 2019 - Dec. 2021</span>
            </div>
          </div>
          <h4 class="sk-entry-subheading">Activation and Adsorption Studies of MOFs and Zeolites</h4>
          <ul class="sk-entry-bullets">
            <li>Performed gas and ion exchange experiments on zeolite single crystals under high-vacuum conditions.</li>
            <li>Developed mild activation protocols for fragile porphyrin-based metal-organic frameworks to improve gas adsorption.</li>
          </ul>
          <h4 class="sk-entry-subheading">Biocompatible Metal–Tartrate MOFs and Their Antibacterial Properties</h4>

          </ul>
